title: Successors of infinite cardinals are regular
statement: Use the smaller universe of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$. For every infinite cardinal $\eta\in\mathcal U$, its successor cardinal $\eta^+$, the least cardinal strictly greater than $\eta$, is an infinite regular cardinal in $\mathcal U$. Here regular means that a union of fewer than $\eta^+$ sets, each of cardinality less than $\eta^+$, has cardinality less than $\eta^+$.

source.place: Cardinal.isRegular_succ, line 79; its hypothesis is aleph0 ≤ eta. Regularity is the usual cardinal regularity. Used for the successor in HTT Definition A.2.6.3, printed p. 819.
